Done. The parser bug was in the lexer, not the Svelte block-parsing code.

## Root cause

In `crates/biome_html_parser/src/lexer/mod.rs`, `consume_restricted_single_text_expression` tracks nested brackets while consuming a key expression that should stop at the outer `)` (`RestrictedExpressionStopAt::ClosingParen`).

The closing-bracket branch was guarded by `&& !kind.matches_punct(current)`. Since `matches_punct(')')` is `true` for the `ClosingParen` kind, **every** `)` skipped this branch — including inner `)` belonging to a nested call like `number.toString()` or `key(number)`. Those inner parens fell through to the catch-all `advance(1)` without ever decrementing `brackets_stack`. The stack stayed unbalanced, so the lexer ran past the intended boundary and produced parse errors / a bogus block.

## Fix

Removed the `!kind.matches_punct` guard on the closing-bracket branch so the stack-depth check alone decides:
- `brackets_stack > 0` → inner closing bracket, decrement and continue (handles the `)` in `toString()` / `key(number)`).
- `brackets_stack == 0` → top-level bracket, which is the stop delimiter (the outer `)`).

This is a targeted, one-branch change. The opening-bracket branch keeps its guard harmlessly (an opening char never matches the `,`/`)` stop puncts), and the `AsOrComma` / `ThenOrCatch` kinds are unaffected since their behavior at those branches is unchanged.

Verified against both required inputs: no parse errors, and each `SVELTE_EACH_KEY` node holds `L_PAREN` + an `HtmlTextExpression`/`HTML_LITERAL` capturing the full call text (`"number.toString()"`, `"key(number)"`) + `R_PAREN`.

Per your instructions I did not touch anything under `tests/` — the test input and snapshot will be applied by the verification system.
